title: New Magic Knight Rayearth Anime's 2nd Main Trailer Reveals More Cast, Theme Songs
content:
The KyoMAF special stage for the new anime of CLAMP 's Magic Knight Rayearth manga on Sunday revealed the second main promotional video and additional cast members for the series. The video also reveals and previews the opening theme song "Otome no Tsurugi" (A Young Lady's Sword) by Toaka , and the ending theme song "Hoshiakari" (Starlight) by Yurina Kawaguchi .

The newly announced cast members are:

Mamiko Noto as Alcione

Ayumu Murase as Ascot

Hitomi Ueda as Caldina

Hiroki Yasumoto as Lafarga

The event also revealed the anime will air for two consecutive cours (quarter of a year) for a half-year run.

The anime will debut on October 7 in the "IMAnimation W" programming block on TV Asahi and affiliated channels at 11:45 p.m. (10:45 a.m. EDT).

The anime will star:

• Ayane Sakura as Hikaru Shidō

• Rumi Ōkubo as Umi Ryūzaki

• Rie Takahashi as Fū Hōōji

• Saori Hayami as Emeraude

• Yūki Ono as Zagato

• Mika Kikuchi as Mokona

• Yūki Kaji as Clef

• Emiri Katō as Presea

• Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Ferio

Yui Miura (episode director for Ninja Kamui , Bullet/Bullet ) is making his series directorial debut with the anime, and E&H production is producing the anime. Shigeru Murakoshi ( Zombie Land Saga , Ninja Kamui , Apocalypse Hotel ) is in charge of the series scripts. Satomi Watabe ( Escha Chron , Aikatsu Friends! ) is designing the characters. Yuki Kajiura , Takumi Ozawa , and Shiho Terada are composing the music. UNLIMITED PRODUCE by TMS is producing the project.

Additional staff members include:

• Assistant Director: Takayuki Sano

• Chief Animation Director: Satomi Watabe

• Rune God Design/Rune God Mechanic Director: Hiroki Mutaguchi

• Art Director: Kazumaru Ando

• Color Key Artist: Chiho Nakamura

• 3D Supervision: Tomohiko Kan

• Compositing Director of Photography: Hitoshi Tamura

• Editing: Keisuke Yanagi

• Sound Director: Shūhei Abe

• Creative Producer: Sunghoo Park

Magic Knight Rayearth centers on three high school girls named Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu. On a class field trip to Tokyo Tower, they are magically transported into the fantasy world of Cephiro. They are immediately greeted by the mage Clef, who tells them that the world is dying after the priest Zagato kidnapped Princess Emeraude, whose prayers maintain the state of the world. Without her singing, Cephiro is on the brink of collapse. Imbued with magical powers as the Magic Knights, Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu must learn how to work together to survive and save Cephiro.

The creative circle CLAMP serialized the Magic Knight Rayearth manga in Kodansha 's Nakayoshi magazine from 1993 to 1996 with six volumes. The manga inspired two television anime seasons, the first running from October 1994 to March 1995, and the second season, titled Magic Knight Rayearth 2 , running from April to November 1995. The manga also inspired a three-episode 1997 original video anime project simply titled Rayearth , featuring an alternate retelling of the story.

Media Blasters first released the television anime on VHS and DVD in the United States. Discotek Media licensed the anime in 2014, and released it as a complete collection on DVD and Blu-ray Disc in 2017. (The release did not include the Rayearth OVA series.)

title: Magic Knight Rayearth 2026 Unveils New Trailer Featuring Theme Songs, Additional Cast
content:
The upcoming Magic Knight Rayearth anime remake unveiled a new trailer that features the opening and ending theme songs and four additional cast members. Toaka performs the opening theme song “Otome no Ken” and the ending theme song “Seira” is performed by Yurina Kawaguchi. E&H production is animating the series, slated to premiere on October 7, 2026.

The voice cast includes:

• Ayane Sakura as Hikaru Shidou

• Rumi Okubo as Umi Ryuuzaki

• Rie Takahashi as Fuu Hououji

• Saori Hayami as Emeraude

• Yuki Ono as Zagato

• Mika Kikuchi as Mokona

• Yuki Kaji as Clef

• Emiri Kato as Presea

• Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Ferio

• Mamiko Noto as Alcyone (NEW)

• Ayumu Murase as Ascot (NEW)

• Hitomi Ueda as Caldina (NEW)

• Hiroki Yasumoto Lafarga (NEW)

Yui Miura is directing the anime, with Shigeru Murakoshi handling the series composition. Satomi Watanabe handles character design, while Yuki Kajiura, Takumi Ozawa, and Shiho Terada compose the music. Magic Knight Rayearth is a Japanese manga series created by CLAMP . It was serialized in the Nakayoshi magazine from November 1993 to February 1995. A sequel was serialized in the same manga magazine from March 1995 to April 1996. Kodansha published both series in a total of 6 volumes, and they describe it as follows: While on a field trip to Tokyo Tower, three teenage girls cross a magical portal and are transported to another world called Cefiro. There they are summoned through the last remaining strength of the Princess Emeraude, who believes the trio will become the magic knights who will save her, as prophesied by legend.

title: New 'Magic Knight Rayearth' Unveils Additional Cast, Theme Songs, Second Promo
content:
The stage event for the new television anime adaptation of CLAMP 's Magic Knight Rayearth at the Kyoto International Manga Anime Fair 2026 unveiled additional cast, the theme songs, and a second promotional video on Sunday. The new anime series is scheduled to premiere on October 7 at 11.45 p.m. on TV Asahi's "IMAnimation W" programming block.

Cast Alcyone: Mamiko Noto ( Kimi ni Todoke ) Ascot: Ayumu Murase ( Chainsaw Man ) Caldina: Hitomi Ueda ( Kekkon Yubiwa Monogatari ) Lafarga: Hiroki Yasumoto ( Koukaku Kidoutai (TV))

Singer-songwriter Toaka ( Suzume no Tojimari ) is performing the opening theme "Otome no Tsurugi." Yurina Kawaguchi is performing the ending theme "Hoshiakari." Both theme songs are previewed in the second promotional video below.

Yui Umemoto ( Ninja Kamui ) is directing at E&H Production , with Takayuki Sano ( Bullet/Bullet episode director) is serving as the assistant director. Shigeru Murakoshi ( Apocalypse Hotel ) is handling the series composition and Satomi Watanabe ( Aikatsu! ) is designing the characters. Yuki Kajiura ( Mahou Shoujo Madoka★Magica ), Takumi Ozawa ( Magia Record: Mahou Shoujo Madoka☆Magica Gaiden ), and Shiho Terada ( Inazuma Eleven Go ) are composing the music.

CLAMP serialized the manga in Nakayoshi magazine from November 1993 to February 1995. A sequel manga began in the same month and ended in March 1996.

Tokyopop licensed both manga in 1997, followed by Dark Horse Comics in 2009, and then Kodansha USA in 2019 with two hard-cover box sets containing three volumes each.

PV 2

title: Roshidere Season 2 Reveals Teaser Trailer
content:
Alya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian (Roshidere) Season 2 revealed a teaser trailer on Sunday. The sequel is slated to premiere in 2027 .

Doga Kobo returns to animate the second season with a new director, Hiroshi Haraguchi, replacing Ryota Itoh. Yuka Yamada is in charge of the series composition while Yuhei Murota is the character designer. The cast will reprise their roles:

• Sumire Uesaka as Alisa Mikhailovna Kujou

• Kohei Amasaki as Masachika Kuze

• Wakana Maruoka as Yuki Suou

• Yukiyo Fuji as Maria Mikhailovna Kujou

• Saya Aizawa as Ayano Kimishima

SunSunSun writes the light novel that the anime is based on, with illustrations by Momoco. There’s also a manga adaptation by Saho Tenamachi. Yen Press licensed the novel and manga in English and they describe the former as follows: Alisa Mikhailovna Kujou is Seiren Private Academy’s “solitary princess.” She’s a half-Russian beauty with silver hair, at the top of her class, student council accountant, and…completely unapproachable. For some reason, she’s also taken on the responsibility of reprimanding the slacker who sits next to her in class. Masachika Kuze is constantly frustrating her by falling asleep, forgetting his textbooks, and just being an overall unexemplary student. Or at least, that’s how it looks from the outside. She may put on a tough act, but she doesn’t mind Masachika as much as others would think. She even lets him call her by her nickname, Alya. Anyone hearing the comments she mutters in Russian under her breath might know how she really feels, but since none of her classmates understand the language, she’s free to say whatever she likes! Except…there is one person who knows what she’s saying. Masachika eavesdrops on her embarrassing revelations, pretending to be clueless, all the while wondering what her flirtatious comments actually mean! Source: Roshidere Official Website © SunSunSun/Momoco/KADOKAWA/Alya-san Partners2

title: Alya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian TV Anime's 2nd Season Reveals Teaser Video
content:
Kadokawa unveiled a new teaser video at the KyoMAF event on Sunday for the second anime season of writer Sunsunsun and artist Momoco 's Alya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian ( Tokidoki Bosotto Russia-go de Dereru Tonari no Alya-san ) light novel series.

Kadokawa also revealed the book franchise has 5.5 million copies in circulation worldwide (including digital copies sold).

The new season was previously slated to debut this year, but was delayed to 2027 to improve the quality of the series.

Hiroshi Haraguchi , the first season's episode 4 director, will direct the second season replacing Ryota Itoh , at Dōga Kōbō . Yuka Yamada , who wrote the script for episode 6, is now in charge of series scripts, also replacing Itoh. Yūhei Murota is again designing the characters. Seong Min Kim , who was a storyboard artist and episode director for the first season, is the assistant director for the new season.

The anime's second season will continue from the light novel's fourth volume.

The first anime season debuted in July 2024 and aired for 12 episodes. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired, and also streams an English dub.

Yen Press is releasing the novels in English, and it describes the story:

Alisa Mikhailovna Kujou is Seiren Private Academy's “solitary princess.” She's a half-Russian beauty with silver hair, at the top of her class, student council accountant, and…completely unapproachable. For some reason, she's also taken on the responsibility of reprimanding the slacker who sits next to her in class. Masachika Kuze is constantly frustrating her by falling asleep, forgetting his textbooks, and just being an overall unexemplary student. Or at least, that's how it looks from the outside. She may put on a tough act, but she doesn't mind Masachika as much as others would think. She even lets him call her by her nickname, Alya. Anyone hearing the comments she mutters in Russian under her breath might know how she really feels, but since none of her classmates understand the language, she's free to say whatever she likes! Except…there is one person who knows what she's saying. Masachika eavesdrops on her embarrassing revelations, pretending to be clueless, all the while wondering what her flirtatious comments actually mean!

Kadokawa publishes the novels under its Sneaker Bunko imprint. Saho Tenamachi ( Shōsetsu no Kami-sama ; Itsuka, Nemuri ni Tsuku Hi ) launched a manga adaptation in October 2022 on Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket app. Yen Press and K MANGA both release the manga in English.
author: ANN

title: 10 Years Later, This Is Still One of Anime’s Most Heartbreaking Movies Ever
content:
The ever-growing popularity of the anime industry in recent years has many curious people looking to venture into the world of exciting shows and movies. While the anime medium has been popular in the U.S. since the 1990s, it continues to grow even now. The 2010s was a transformative era for the anime industry since it continued after the finale of the Shonen Big Three. Not to mention that the long-running anime series quickly began to disappear while the seasonal releases took over. In terms of anime movies, the quick rise of the medium resulted in more theatrical releases across the U.S. and in several regions outside of Japan.

One such anime that made its mark during that era was Kyoto Animation’s A Silent Voice , which is still one of the most beloved and heartbreaking movies of all time. The anime is based on Yoshitoki Ooiama’s award-winning Weekly Shonen Jump manga, which was serialized from 2013 to 2014. The anime premiered in Japan on September 16th, 2026, but made its theatrical debut in the U.S. on October 20th, 2017. Earlier this year, Crunchyroll made it easier for fans across the globe to watch this movie, proving how well-loved it is even now.

What Is A Silent Voice About?

This heart-wrenching story centers around Shoya Ishida, who spends his days drowning his guilt for what he did in childhood. Along with his friends, he bullied Shoko Nishimiya, a hearing-impaired girl, when they were both in elementary school. The bullying was so extreme that he wouldn’t hesitate to take off her hearing aid, which would make her ears bleed. Not to mention that she relied heavily on those expensive aids. The bullying got so severe that she had no choice but to transfer out of school.

However, Shoya never would’ve expected that when the truth came out, all his friends would put the blame on him. It didn’t take long for him to become the target of bullying, which led him to become even more isolated. He became completely ostracized after the incident and never managed to rid himself of the guilt of what he did to Shoko. Now in high school, he struggles with self-loathing and anxiety while seeking redemption. He tracks down Shoko to apologize and tries to make amends for the past.

Although he wasn’t expecting her to forgive him, Shoko accepts his apology, and the two slowly rebuild their friendship while struggling with personal scars. As he learns more about the girl, he realizes that even as a teenager, Shoko still feels inadequate after facing countless hardships. Along the way, he also reunites with his elementary school classmates who have moved on with their lives after everything that happened.

A Silent Voice Is One of the Most Heartbreaking Stories of Redemption

This stunning film touches on some sensitive themes while focusing on redemption and forgiveness. After their reunion, the story focuses on the duo’s emotional burden, creating moments of vulnerability as they focus on healing. Shoya’s heartbreaking journey of redemption and Shoko’s path of self-acceptance culminate in a touching and emotional ending. What truly makes this movie special is how it highlights the importance of meaningful connections with others.

While the anime film covers the main storyline within all seven manga volumes, it significantly condenses the narrative and cuts down major subplots, including side character development, to fit the runtime. This means that the manga will never get a full adaptation, but that doesn’t diminish the movie’s greatness. Even so, the film’s ending is fairly conclusive and leaves no room for doubt as the main duo finds solace in each other’s company. The ending is perhaps one of the best visual representations seen in anime movies.

Instead of directly depicting Shoya’s healing journey, it focuses on his personal transformation as the metaphorical “X” marks from those around him begin to drop. The “X” marks were simply what he viewed on others’ faces to symbolize his deep social anxiety, intense guilt, and self-imposed isolation. However, the finale confirmed he is breaking out of his shell, which was a major part of his healing process. Additionally, Shoko finally learns to accept herself for who she is and live alongside others without feeling inadequate.

title: Shonen Jump Hit Confirms Crunchyroll Return Date for New Season After Finale – Watch Trailer
content:
The Fall 2026 anime season is right around the corner, and it’s going to be the biggest quarter of this year. 2026 has been a considerably exciting year for fans with the return of many major shows, including Jujutsu Kaisen, Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End , and more. No doubt that the Fall 2026 lineup doesn’t plan to disappoint since fans are already anticipating the return of Black Clover and The Apothecary Diaries . Among the anticipated sequels, the new season of The Prince of Tennis is all set for its Crunchyroll premiere. It’s one of the longest-running series on Shonen Jump since the manga was split into two parts.

title: 10 Things I Want to Do Before I Turn 40 Boys-Love Manga Also Gets Live-Action Film
content:
The staff for the live-action series of Mamita 's 10 Things I Want to Do Before I Turn 40 ( 40 Made ni Shitai 10 no Koto ) boys-love manga announced on Saturday that the manga is also receving a live-action film on January 22, 2027. The cast of the TV series are reprising their roles for the film.

Chihiro Ikeda returns to direct the film based on a screenplay by Yō Saitō.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the manga, and released the first volume on May 6. The company describes the story:

Suzume Tōjō is just three months away from turning forty and realizes there's so much he hasn't done with his life! So, he makes a plan: create a private list of things he's always wanted to do and check them off before turning the big four-oh. It's a rather simple list, filled with goals that should be easy to accomplish, like a takoyaki party, enjoying a parfait out in a cafe, and spending his birthday with a lover. Except, that last one comes with a major problem--Tōjō hasn't had a lover in ten years! But when Keishi Tanaka, Tōjō's handsome junior at the company, discovers the secret list, he's determined to help Tōjō check off every single item--starting with the "lover" part!

Kōhei Shōji plays Keishi Tanaka, while Shunsuke Kazama plays Suzume Tōjō.

Ikeda (live-action Senpai to Kanojo , Kowloon Generic Romance ) and Noriaki Kosuge (co-director of Yo-kai Watch: Sora Tobu Kujira to Double Sekai no Daibōken da Nyan! live-action segment) directed the series, with scripts by Saitō (Aibō) . Erina Koyama (live-action Kowloon Generic Romance ) composed the music.

The live-action series premiered on the TV Tokyo , TV Osaka , TV Aichi , TV Setouchi , TV Hokkaido , and TVQ channels on July 4, 2025 and also streamed on Lemino , U-NEXT , TV Tokyo HP, and TVer services in Japan.

Mamita launched the manga in Libre Publishing 's Be x Boy magazine in 2022. Libre Publishing released the manga's second and final volume on February 19, 2025.

Seven Seas is also releasing Mamita 's Wanna Be My Dress-Up Lover? and Natsume Wants to be Trained manga. SuBLime previously released Mamita 's The Metalhead Next Door manga.

title: Winners of Next Manga Award 2026 Announced
content:
The winners of Kadokawa 's annual Next Manga Award were announced on Wednesday. The awards ceremony was streamed on Niconico on the same day. Out of the 7,952 titles that were submitted for the award, 100 titles (40 print manga, 60 web manga) were nominated by a special commitee for the final round of voting. A total of 382,581 votes were cast by fans this year.

Print Manga 1. Someone Hertz 2. Futari Bus 3. Register! 4. Parashoppers 5. Silver Mountain 6. Manemane Nichinichi 7. Yamero Suki ni Natteshimau 8. Koi to Yobu ni wa Sasayaka desu ga 9. Roku no Okashi na Ie 10. Shachou to Sake to Hoshi

11. Kurotsuki no Yaergnacht 12. Rou Warai 13. Kesa mo Yuraretemasu 14. Oshiete Shitsuji-kun 15. Konzukushi 16. 2-nen B-gumi Yuusha Destroyers 17. Dig It 18. Houkago Kitaku Biyori 19. Osananananajimi 20. Tsutte Tabetai Gal Sawa-san

Web Manga 1. Okaeri Suiheisen 2. Hitoner 3. Haimiya-senpai wa Kowakute Kawaii 4. Otona Taisen 5. Toshi Densetsu-senpai 6. Haruno-san no Koto nante Zenzen Suki 7. Idolatry 8. Kurumizawa Yoshihiko no Gukou 9. WITCHRIV 10. Kaisha to Shiseikatsu: On to Off

11. Tonari no Seki no Yatsu ga Souiu Me de Mitekuru 12. Seikatsu Man 13. Blue Archive: Game Kaihatsu-bu Daibouken! 14. Kami Yomu Futari 15. Daiakutou Shounen 16. Hatori to Furuta no Hinichijou Sahanji 17. Moriagaranai Date 18. Bateren Kaidan 19. Harem Yuusha Densetsu 20. Tachinomi Izakaya de Kuudere Downer-kei Joshidaisei ga Tonari ni Kuru Hanashi

Special Awards Dig It (U-Next Award, Print Manga) WITCHRIV (U-Next Award, Web Manga) Kyoukai no Melody (Nichirei Foods Award) Jimi na Ojisan, Jitsu wa Eiyuu deshita. Jikaku ga Nai Mama Musou shitetara, Mei no Dungeon Haishin de Sarasareteta you desu (Niconico Manga Award)

The annual Next Manga Award (Tsugi ni Kuru Manga Taishou) was established in 2014 by Kadokawa's Da Vinci magazine and the streaming platform Niconico. The award aims to discover and introduce new titles, with the two categories initially labeled as "Manga We Want to See Become a Hit" and "Web Manga We Want to See Published as a Book." Titles that are eligible for the award are required to be serialized in a magazine and they either have to begin their serialization the previous year, or have no more than five volumes released. The top three titles in each category enter the Hall of Fame and become ineligible to enter future Next Manga Award.

title: Dragon Ball Super Fans Bring Black Frieza to Life Ahead of the Villain’s Anime Return – Watch Now
content:
Dragon Ball Super is currently in the works on coming back with a new anime picking up with the missing arcs of the manga, but a special fan animation has brought Black Frieza to life as they are looking forward to seeing this moment hit the official anime release. Dragon Ball Super is setting up for a huge anime comeback for the franchise as a new remake anime series will be premiering this Fal l and taking on the TV anime series all the way back to the beginning.

This is all leading to the eventual return of Dragon Ball Super with brand new stories. It’s now in the works on a new anime adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc , and it’s just one of the two arcs left from the manga that the anime can take on. But fans are hoping to see the anime get to Black Frieza sooner rather than later, and that’s especially true for artists like D VINCHY who took to social media to share a cool anime take on the fight between Black Frieza and Gas. Check it out in action below.

When Does Dragon Ball Super’s New Anime Come Out?

Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol is now in the works, but no concrete release window or date has been announced as of the time of this writing. This new anime is going to be picking up from the events of the original TV anime and Dragon Ball Super: Broly movie, and continuing with the adaptation of the Dragon Ball Super manga illustrated by Toyotaro. As teased by the title, it’s going to be adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc from the manga release with the introduction of Planet Eater Moro as the next big villain.

Black Frieza specifically comes from the arc after this with Dragon Ball Super’ s Granolah the Survivor arc. Without getting too much into how the villain makes his comeback to the franchise, the villain’s return is still the lingering question that fans have had ever since the manga went on hiatus. It’s been two years since the manga went on hiatus following its adaptation of the Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero movie, and it still needs to lead into the fallout of what’s going to happen to Goku and the others now that Frieza is the most powerful fighter in the universe .

What’s Next for Dragon Ball Super?

There’s going to be some new Dragon Ball Super to watch this Fall ahead of the new arc thanks to a new remake series kicking off its run this October. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus goes all the way back to the Battle of Gods arc , and will be showing off an enhanced version of the original TV anime series. Fans will get to see new versions of the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F, and Universe 6 arcs this Fall, and it should be the perfect way to get up to speed before the new anime hits in the future.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be making its debut on October 11th in Japan, but it has yet to confirm international release plans or streaming home as of the time of this writing. But there should be a new update on that front soon enough as Toei Animation will be hosting a special panel during New York Comic Con 2026 on October 8th that will be hosted by Monica Rial (English dub voice of Bulma) with Jason Douglas (English dub voice of Beerus) and Ian Sinclair (English dub voice of Whis) attending as special guests.
